title: Getting started with the Mosquito Weather Index
text: Mosquito Weather Index reduces three weather variables one number [0, 1]. product three response functions, returns suitability multiplier one variable: shapes worth knowing, explain index’s behaviour. mwi_temperature() trapezoid, flat maximal 20 25 °C zero outside 15–30 °C: mwi_humidity() ramps linearly 40% 95%, drops zero step: step 95% deliberate, artefact. practical consequence: index reaches 1 humidity exactly 95%, top “high activity” class attained rounded observational data almost never continuous data reanalysis output. mwi_wind() switch rather gradient: three responses multiplied, one hitting zero takes whole index . Wind humidity therefore best thought gates, temperature thing grades result.
code: mwi_temperature(22) #> [1] 1 mwi_humidity(70) #> [1] 0.5454545 mwi_wind(10) #> [1] 1  mwi_temperature(22) * mwi_humidity(70) * mwi_wind(10) #> [1] 0.5454545 mwi(temperature = 22, humidity = 70, wind_speed = 10) #> [1] 0.5454545 t <- seq(10, 35, by = 5) data.frame(temperature = t, response = mwi_temperature(t)) #>   temperature response #> 1          10        0 #> 2          15        0 #> 3          20        1 #> 4          25        1 #> 5          30        0 #> 6          35        0 h <- c(35, 40, 60, 80, 95, 96) data.frame(humidity = h, response = mwi_humidity(h)) #>   humidity  response #> 1       35 0.0000000 #> 2       40 0.0000000 #> 3       60 0.3636364 #> 4       80 0.7272727 #> 5       95 1.0000000 #> 6       96 0.0000000 mwi_wind_threshold() #> [1] 21.6 mwi_wind(c(21.5, 21.6, 21.7)) #> [1] 1 1 0

title: Getting started with the Mosquito Weather Index
text: part often goes wrong. mwi() non-linear, commute averaging. hourly weather want daily index, must evaluate index hourly summarise resulting index values. Summarising weather first indexing gives different answer. problem worst daily maxima, daily maximum relative humidity daily maximum temperature fall opposite ends day — humidity peaks small hours, temperature mid-afternoon. Combining describes hour never occurred. mwi_summarise() enforces correct order. Group get one row per day:
code: hours <- 0:23 temperature <- 18 + 8 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi) humidity <- 75 - 15 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi) wind_speed <- rep(5, 24)  # Note the phase difference: they peak twelve hours apart c(warmest_hour = which.max(temperature) - 1,   most_humid_hour = which.max(humidity) - 1) #>    warmest_hour most_humid_hour  #>              12               0 # Right: index each hour, then reduce mwi_summarise(temperature, humidity, wind_speed,               by = rep("2019-07-15", 24), statistic = "max") #>           by       mwi  n #> 1 2019-07-15 0.5657766 24  # Wrong: reduce the weather, then index mwi(max(temperature), max(humidity), max(wind_speed)) #> [1] 0.7272727 two_days <- rep(as.Date(c("2019-07-15", "2019-07-16")), each = 24) mwi_summarise(rep(temperature, 2), rep(humidity, 2), rep(wind_speed, 2),               by = two_days) #>           by       mwi  n #> 1 2019-07-15 0.5657766 24 #> 2 2019-07-16 0.5657766 24

title: Getting started with the Mosquito Weather Index
text: available statistic. evaluation study accompanying package, daily maximum consistently predicted adult trap counts better daily mean, consistent catch responding whether day contained window favourable conditions rather favourable day average.
code: by <- rep("2019-07-15", 24) rbind(   mwi_summarise(temperature, humidity, wind_speed, by, statistic = "max"),   mwi_summarise(temperature, humidity, wind_speed, by, statistic = "mean"),   mwi_summarise(temperature, humidity, wind_speed, by, statistic = "min") ) #>           by       mwi  n #> 1 2019-07-15 0.5657766 24 #> 2 2019-07-15 0.2405692 24 #> 3 2019-07-15 0.0000000 24

code: x <- c(0, 0.15, 0.5, 0.85, 1) data.frame(mwi = x, class = mwi_category(x)) #>    mwi              class #> 1 0.00        No activity #> 2 0.15       Low activity #> 3 0.50  Moderate activity #> 4 0.85      High activity #> 5 1.00 Very high activity mwi_category(0.85) > mwi_category(0.15) #> [1] TRUE greek <- c("Καμία", "Χαμηλή", "Μέτρια", "Υψηλή", "Πολύ υψηλή") mwi_category(c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = greek) #> [1] Καμία      Μέτρια     Πολύ υψηλή #> Levels: Καμία < Χαμηλή < Μέτρια < Υψηλή < Πολύ υψηλή

what: Feeding the index from reanalysis data
title: Getting started with the Mosquito Weather Index
text: Gridded products rarely give three variables form index wants. ERA5-Land, instance, distributes 2 m air temperature 2 m dewpoint Kelvin, 10 m wind eastward northward components m/s. conversions included:
code: t2m <- c(295.15, 299.15, 291.15) d2m <- c(288.15, 289.15, 287.15) u10 <- c(1.2, -3.4, 0.5) v10 <- c(-0.8, 2.1, 1.1)  temperature <- celsius_from_kelvin(t2m) dewpoint <- celsius_from_kelvin(d2m) humidity <- relative_humidity_from_dewpoint(dewpoint, temperature) wind_speed <- wind_speed_from_components(u10, v10)  data.frame(   temperature = round(temperature, 1),   humidity = round(humidity, 1),   wind_ms = round(wind_speed, 1),   mwi = round(mwi(temperature, humidity, wind_speed, units = "m/s"), 3) ) #>   temperature humidity wind_ms   mwi #> 1          22     64.5     1.4 0.446 #> 2          26     54.1     4.0 0.205 #> 3          18     77.5     1.2 0.409

text: Temperature humidity loggers measure wind. mwi_fhft() drops wind term, equivalent assuming wind always cut-: Treat variant care. evaluation study found substituting -site logger readings gridded reanalysis made index worse predictor trap counts, partly logger humidity ran systematically dry 40% threshold amplifies bias.
code: mwi_fhft(temperature = 22, humidity = 70) #> [1] 0.5454545 mwi(temperature = 22, humidity = 70, wind_speed = 0) #> [1] 0.5454545

title: Getting started with the Mosquito Weather Index
text: Every function propagates NA rather guessing: mwi_summarise(), group containing missing index value returns NA unless ask otherwise: Note arguments must length length 1. Partial recycling error rather silent surprise:
code: mwi(temperature = c(22, NA), humidity = 70, wind_speed = 5) #> [1] 0.5454545        NA gappy_temperature <- 18 + 8 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi) gappy_temperature[5] <- NA gappy_humidity <- 75 - 15 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi)  mwi_summarise(gappy_temperature, gappy_humidity, rep(5, 24), by)$mwi #> [1] NA mwi_summarise(gappy_temperature, gappy_humidity, rep(5, 24), by,               na.rm = TRUE)$mwi #> [1] 0.5657766 mwi(temperature = c(20, 22, 24, 26), humidity = c(60, 70), wind_speed = 5) #> Error: #> ! Arguments must have the same length or length 1. Got `humidity` (2) against a common length of 4.

title: Compute the Mosquito Weather Index
text: Mosquito Weather Index (MWI) combines air temperature, relative humidity wind speed single number 0 1 describing favourable weather adult mosquito activity, maps number onto five ordered activity classes. developed Benaki Phytopathological Institute National Observatory Athens LIFE CONOPS project (LIFE12 ENV/GR/000466) published operationally meteo.gr since June 2014. package implements index, three response functions built , activity classes, unit conversions needed feed common weather products. dependencies beyond base R. Full documentation, including worked introduction, https://e4warning.github.io/mwi/.

title: Compute the Mosquito Weather Index
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("E4Warning/mwi")

title: Compute the Mosquito Weather Index
text: index product three responses, one variable falling outside favourable range sets whole index zero: individual responses available : Continuous values map onto five classes used public communication:
code: library(mwi)  mwi(temperature = 22, humidity = 70, wind_speed = 10) #> [1] 0.5454545 mwi(temperature = 22, humidity = 30, wind_speed = 10) # too dry #> [1] 0 mwi(temperature = 35, humidity = 70, wind_speed = 10) # too hot #> [1] 0 mwi(temperature = 22, humidity = 70, wind_speed = 30) # too windy #> [1] 0 mwi_temperature(c(10, 17.5, 22, 27.5, 32)) #> [1] 0.0 0.5 1.0 0.5 0.0 mwi_humidity(c(30, 40, 67.5, 95)) #> [1] 0.0 0.0 0.5 1.0 mwi_wind(c(10, 21.6, 25)) #> [1] 1 1 0 x <- c(0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.9, 1) data.frame(mwi = x, class = mwi_category(x)) #>   mwi              class #> 1 0.0        No activity #> 2 0.2       Low activity #> 3 0.5  Moderate activity #> 4 0.9      High activity #> 5 1.0 Very high activity

title: Compute the Mosquito Weather Index
text: index must computed averaged, . mwi() non-linear, evaluating daily summaries weather variable evaluating hourly summarising result — much less useful. Daily maxima temperature humidity typically occur many hours apart, index built describes hour never happened. mwi_summarise() right order:
code: hours <- 0:23 temp <- 18 + 8 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi) rh <- 75 - 15 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi) wind <- rep(5, 24)  # Right: index each hour, then take the daily maximum mwi_summarise(temp, rh, wind, by = rep("2019-07-15", 24)) #>           by       mwi  n #> 1 2019-07-15 0.5657766 24  # Wrong: summarise the weather first, then index mwi(max(temp), max(rh), max(wind)) #> [1] 0.7272727

text: Computes Mosquito Weather Index (MWI), operational index combines air temperature, relative humidity wind speed single number 0 1 summarising favourable weather adult mosquito activity, maps number onto five ordered activity classes. index developed Benaki Phytopathological Institute National Observatory Athens LIFE CONOPS project published operationally since 2014. index non-linear function three inputs, must evaluated sub-daily resolution aggregated time; helpers provided enforce order operations.

title: Summarise sub-daily weather into index values, in the correct order — mwi_summarise
text: index product non-linear response functions, commute averaging: mwi(mean(temperature), mean(humidity), mean(wind)) mean(mwi(temperature, humidity, wind)). discrepancy severe daily maxima, daily maximum relative humidity daily maximum temperature usually fall many hours apart, index computed describes conditions never co-occurred. mwi_summarise() therefore takes sub-daily observations, evaluates mwi() one, reduces results statistic within level . Empirically maximum informative summary: captures whether period contained window favourable conditions, rather favourable period average.

title: Summarise sub-daily weather into index values, in the correct order — mwi_summarise
code: # One synthetic day of hourly weather hours <- 0:23 temp <- 18 + 8 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi) rh <- 75 - 15 * sin((hours - 6) / 24 * 2 * pi) wind <- rep(5, 24)  mwi_summarise(temp, rh, wind, by = rep("2019-07-15", 24)) #>           by       mwi  n #> 1 2019-07-15 0.5657766 24  # The wrong order gives a different answer mwi(max(temp), max(rh), max(wind)) #> [1] 0.7272727

title: mwi 0.1.0
text: Initial public release, accompanying article Evaluating Mosquito Weather Index: simple tool predicting communicating mosquito activity (submitted). mwi() implements Mosquito Weather Index operationally defined LIFE CONOPS project, three weather-response functions (mwi_temperature(), mwi_humidity(), mwi_wind()) temperature--humidity-variant mwi_fhft(). mwi_category() maps index values onto five operational activity classes; mwi_activity_levels() returns labels. mwi_summarise() aggregates sub-daily weather order index requires: computed sub-daily resolution first, summarised. Conversions reanalysis inputs: relative_humidity_from_dewpoint() (Magnus approximation), wind_speed_from_components(), celsius_from_kelvin(). Validated article’s analysis pipeline: test suite includes 314 hourly ERA5-Land observations study pipeline-computed reference values, stratified across every regime every response function.
